title: Why Greece Stayed Divided
question: Why was Greece a patchwork of city-states instead of one country?
hook: For nearly all of its ancient history, Greece was not one country, and its landscape and history help explain why.
idea: The absence of powerful states and a mountainous landscape that separated settlements encouraged small independent city-states.

beats.prompt: The Mycenaean powers have collapsed, and Greek settlements sit in valleys separated by mountains. What kind of political units will grow up?

choices.label: One kingdom ruling the whole region
choices.feedback: A single ruler sounds natural, but no powerful state remained after the collapse and mountains kept settlements apart.

choices.label: Cities all answering to a foreign empire
choices.feedback: Outside rule is tempting, but the lack of any powerful state pushed the cities toward independence.

beats.explain: With no powerful states and many settlements separated by mountains, small independent city-states developed.

beats.prompt: Put these stages of Greek history in order.
beats.explain: The Dark Ages came first, then the Archaic period, then the Classical period, and the Hellenistic period followed.

beats.prompt: Match each name to what it is known for.
pairs: Famous example of the classical style
Spread Greek culture into Northern Africa and Western Asia
beats.explain: Each is tied to a different part of the Greek story: writing history, a classical style, the spread of culture and the city-state.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: The Archaic period came before the Classical period.
Most of the Greek area was unified only once before the Roman period.
So a single Greek kingdom ruled for most of the Archaic and Classical periods.
Therefore early Greek history is mostly about separate city-states.
beats.explain: The area was unified only once, from 338 to 323 BC, so for most of the Archaic and Classical periods there was no single Greek kingdom.
